title: [Performance][DCP] Refresh native decode layouts and remap fixes for main
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reduce layout, copy and cache-publication overhead around native SFA DCP decode, continuing #16349 on main. The registered entry remains `dcp_a2a_fused`.

- **Output/LSE exchange:** pack BF16 partial output `[T, H, D]` and FP32 LSE `[T, H, 1]` as raw bits, perform one AllToAll, merge in FP32, and return BF16 `[T, H / R, D]`. `T` is the query-token count seen by the operator, including padding; it is not context length. Dimensions and head shards come from the inputs and group. Small payloads retain the existing full-vector kernels; larger output/LSE payloads use bounded native head/feature tiles with tokens distributed across Vector Cores. The 16K-element threshold selects tiling, not a fixed token cap or upstream fallback. Existing power-of-two/layout constraints remain; D512/local-head32 and scheduler-budget/T192 admission limits have been removed.
- **Query gather:** derive NoPE/RoPE fragment widths and head counts from inputs; preserve split sizes in the gather context and honor `keep_view`. Eligible power-of-two fragments support BF16/FP16/FP32, without the old 512/64 or T=2–12 whitelist. Other layouts retain the existing preparation path.
- **Sparse-index remap:** use exact bit operations for power-of-two DCP/interleave settings without narrowing INT64 indices. Other settings use exact INT64 Torch arithmetic and stable compaction; sorting may involve AICPU.
- **Native LI-C8 cache store:** combine final INT8 key publication and FP16 scale conversion/publication at the existing cache-write point. Native quantization and its rounding are unchanged. PCP/DSA-CP and other cache formats keep their existing routes.

The native exchange route uses the same tensor/group/mode contract across NPU generations. PCP composition, token scatter, returned-LSE and deferred-combine modes retain their existing implementations. In the current normal SFA prefill path, including PCP+DCP prefill, KV is gathered and attention returns before the decode O/LSE merge; a large prefill `T` does not by itself exercise this decode pack kernel.

Operator interfaces, constraints and numerical semantics are documented under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/` in `sfa_dcp_exchange.md`, `sfa_dcp_merge.md`, `sfa_dcp_query.md` and `sfa_indexer_store.md`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: faster DCP decode components, exact large-index remapping, bounded native packing for larger eligible inputs, and single-token dtype-view compatibility. There is no new serving API, environment variable or scheduler-budget parameter, and no change to SuperMem allocation/placement.

Release note: [`release_notes/fragments/16350.yaml`](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm-ascend/blob/codex/dcp-decode-layouts/release_notes/fragments/16350.yaml).

### How was this patch tested?

**Current runtime code: `7df9b3375`.** The release-note follow-up changes metadata only.

- CPU routing, dependency, exact-integer and specialization contracts: **705 passed, 20 skipped**.
- Fresh A3 DCP2/4/8: **10 cases passed on every rank** for each group, including T512/513, T256/257, T1025, wide outputs, changing-input ACLGraph replay and revisiting older captures. The large-vector tests assert that the native path is used.
- Single-card tiled-pack precision: **6 passed**, checking both LSE storage layouts and exact BF16/FP32 bits, including NaN payloads, Inf and negative zero.
- Single-token ordinary, odd-singleton and odd-offset layouts pass graph replay. The odd-singleton failure was reproduced with a constructed tensor; the actual SFA producer returned normal strides and worked on all eight ranks. This is not a claim that normal T1 model requests were failing.
- Changed-file manual pre-commit and targeted typing checks passed. The [CI run for `7df9b3375`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40855000062) also passed its CI gate, including selected A2/A3/A5/310P tests. CI coverage is separate from the manual benchmarks below.

The fresh operator runs reused the existing A3 runtime: Python 3.12, Torch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, Triton 3.2.0 and vLLM `ced6857.empty`; msprof was from the CANN 9.1 installation. This is not a fresh full-model or default-dependency validation.

**Matched complete-path performance:** previous optimized PR head `65163ad6e` versus `7df9b3375`, including pack → AllToAll → merge → final BF16 output.

| A3 configuration | Previous PR | Tiled pack | Latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DCP8 / H64 / D512 / T192 | 206.651 us | 207.101 us | +0.22% |
| DCP2 / H64 / D512 / T513 | 1319.364 us | 529.044 us | −59.90% |

External msprof `op_summary`, 10 alternating-order pairs ×50 replays per mode: take the slowest rank per replay, then the median per block and across 10 blocks. No outliers were removed. T513 compares against the previous **upstream fallback**; the earlier unbounded native pack failed to compile at this shape. T192 still uses the unchanged small-input pack kernels. These are operator graph intervals, not HTTP TPOT or full-model throughput.

The original decode-overhead objective is supported by earlier A3 upstream OFF→ON evidence at `ec9b9a786`: T48 **181.37→98.03us** and T192 **528.19→203.17us**. Those historical results remain tied to that revision; the current table checks the later change against the already optimized PR.

**Specialization and warmup:** `LSE_RANK_STRIDE` remains a measured constexpr exception and can create new merge variants for unseen actual shapes. In the previously tested `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, no-MTP/no-LoRA, DP1/max batch 192 setup, buckets `[1,2,4,8,16,32,48,64,96,128,192]` cover normal single-token decode batches 1–192 through padding. A CPU enumeration of the actual dispatch methods at both `ced6857` and `544f182` confirmed that mapping; it is not a fresh all-batch model run. Uncovered eager shapes can still compile on first use, and disk-cache loading still has startup cost. See the [focused compilation check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16350#issuecomment-6491005525); this PR does not claim token-independent or zero-compilation serving for arbitrary configurations.

**Earlier model evidence, with revision boundaries:**

- A3 GLM-5.2 W4A8, optimization ON at `6a8c6c0f8`: official AISBench community `gsm8k-lite`, **31/32 (96.875%)**, within its 95±5 reference gate; TP8/DCP8/EP8/MRV2, no MTP/offload/prefix cache. The checkpoint did not select the LI-C8 store path, so this does not validate model-level INT8 cache writes.
- A5 full 78-layer GLM-5 MXW4A8 at `5a7bf962` versus base `6ba8bc2d`: GSM8K first 32 examples **31/32→32/32**, and offline generation throughput medians **+0.66% to +2.16%** on shared hardware. This is a smoke subset with small performance deltas, not full-dataset certification or a current-head model rerun. See the [A5 operator validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16350#issuecomment-6396296753) and [A5 model follow-up](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16350#issuecomment-6408325712).

Fresh current-head full-model accuracy/performance, full GPQA, model-level LI-C8 and DCP16 are not claimed by these checks. Large-shape probes establish operator behavior, not that a complete checkpoint fits HBM at every tested shape.

Relevant test commands:

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_dcp.py
python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_sfa_dcp.py -k tiled_pack
# Repeat with nproc-per-node=2,4,8 in isolated NPU environments.
python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 \
  -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/multicard_ops_a3/test_sfa_dcp.py \
  -k 'singleton_stride or tiled_resource'
```
